Every one of them passes in isolation on both heads. No failure is attributable to the PR79B changes; the PR79B run adds 47 passing tests and removes one base-head flake.

deliberate_non_claims: No protocol-level SSE Last-Event-ID replay of JSON-RPC message streams: the supported server configuration is stateless streamable HTTP with JSON responses, where the SDK event-store seam is not wired. Durable resume is exposed as the typed marker_events surface backed by the kernel semantic sequence.
No exactly-once network delivery claim; resume is at-least-once with stable semantic_sequence identity for deterministic de-duplication.
No OIDC verifier, group membership, enterprise document ACL, or per-principal workspace ACL. principal_id is a transport caller binding inside the existing local_v1 authorization model.
stdio and loopback no-auth transports have no server-validated identity; cursors there are explicitly unbound local capabilities.
Without stable key material (MARKER_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY or ENCRYPTION_KEY), cursor keys are ephemeral per process and chains die with the process; this is logged.
Pre-PR79B cursor rows (NULL principal_id) remain caller-agnostic by design.
PR80 extraction/review statuses, PR81 visual/vector retrieval, and PR83 PostgreSQL/object-store work remain deferred.
